title: Change a user’s password
purpose: Replace the selected user’s password as an administrator.
summary: Set a new password for the selected user, or turn their password sign-in off or on.

tasks.title: Set a new password
steps: If [[Confirm it is you]] is shown, type your own password in [[Your password]], and a code from your authenticator app if it asks for one.
Select [[Change password]]. You return to the user's account.

tasks.title: Turn off password sign-in
steps: Choose Disabled under [[Password-based authentication]] and select [[Disable password-based authentication]].

good_to_know: This changes the user named on the page, not necessarily you. No email is sent to them.
Saving asks for your own password, and a code if you have an authenticator app, unless you confirmed in this browser in the last 5 minutes. Each change is audited without passwords.
Turning off password sign-in does not remove two-factor authentication or add another sign-in method.
The password needs at least 15 characters, or 8 if the laboratory requires a second sign-in factor of this account. The form states which.

sections.title: Access and identity
paragraphs: The administration site requires an active account with Staff status. User and group pages additionally require Superuser status; a laboratory admin role alone or individual model permissions do not open them. These technical flags do not themselves confer operational roles or capabilities.

This form identifies the target username and operates on that user, not necessarily the signed-in administrator. It requires user-change permission under the project’s superuser-only account administration.

items.label: Password-based authentication
items.description: Shown only when the target already has a usable password. Enabled is initially selected; Disabled removes usable password authentication and loses the old password. An account with an unusable password has no selector here and is being enabled.

items.label: Password / Password confirmation
items.description: Required matching replacement when enabling or keeping Enabled. The help under it states the rule for this account: at least 15 characters, or 8 where the laboratory's second sign-in factor rule covers the account, read when the password is checked, just before it is saved. Common and expected passwords (a common password or a name of the laboratory, the application or the account with only digits, symbols, spaces or letter case changed, one character or a text of fewer than 15 characters repeated, a run) and ones too similar to the account's details are refused, as is a password marked as compromised for the account. No required kinds of character. Password fields are not required when disabling.

items.label: Your password
items.description: Under Confirm it is you, before the buttons, while saving asks for it, and shown when your account has a password: your own current password, not the user's. The help under it says what saving asks for and that you are not asked again in this browser for 5 minutes. Left empty: Enter your password to save this change. Not accepted: Incorrect password.

items.label: Authenticator or recovery code
items.description: Under Confirm it is you, shown when your account has an authenticator app: a code from it, or one of your unused recovery codes, which is then used up. Left empty: Enter a code from your authenticator app, or a recovery code, to save this change. Not accepted: Incorrect code. The password is checked first; when it is not accepted, the code is not checked and can still be used.

sections.title: Confirm it is you
paragraphs: Change password, Disable password-based authentication and Enable password-based authentication all ask you, the person signed in, to confirm it is you, unless you already confirmed in this browser in the last 5 minutes. Nothing is saved until what you type under Confirm it is you is accepted. Signing in does not count: only confirming again does. Once you have confirmed, no page that asks (account administration, and the session limits and second sign-in factor rule on Security settings) asks again in this browser for 5 minutes. A page opened while you were confirmed and saved after the 5 minutes passed asks then.

Confirming on Confirm your password, or with a code before a change to your own two-factor settings, counts too, once you have confirmed every factor your account has within the same 5 minutes; a confirmation here counts for those pages as well. An authenticator app added to your account after you confirmed makes the next save ask again, for both. An account with neither a password nor an authenticator app cannot confirm, so it cannot save here until it sets a password.

When the confirmation is missing or not accepted, nothing is saved, and no audit event or administration history entry is written. The new password fields are emptied, as on any refused save, so type the new password again. A confirmation accepted while the new password is refused is kept: the page shows the password's error without the section, and saving again within the 5 minutes does not ask.

A password or code not accepted is listed in your own Sign-in history as Re-authentication failed and counts toward the failed sign-in limit; an attempt that limit refuses is listed as Too many failed attempts. What you type under Confirm it is you is never stored, logged or put in an audit event.

items.label: Too many failed login attempts. Try again later.
items.description: The failed sign-in limit refused your password or code before checking it, after too many that were not accepted. Wait a few minutes, then try again.

items.label: Too many attempts to confirm it is you. Wait a minute, then try again.
items.description: Shown after 10 tries within a minute by your account (the Confirm your password pages count too). Nothing was checked, and the refusal is not listed in Sign-in history.

items.label: Your account has no password to confirm it is you, so this change cannot be saved. Set a password on Change password first.
items.description: Your account has neither a password nor an authenticator app, so it has nothing to confirm with. Set a password from Change password in the account menu, then save again.

items.label: Your sign-in factors changed while this page was open. Confirm it is you again.
items.description: An authenticator app was added to or removed from your account while your save was being checked. Nothing is saved or confirmed. Save again: the page then asks for what your account has now.

items.label: Change password
items.description: Shown for a currently usable password; once you have confirmed it is you (see Confirm it is you), applies the enabled replacement after validation and returns to the target’s change form. A new password lifts a mark of the password as compromised; disabling password-based authentication does not.

items.label: Disable password-based authentication
items.description: Shown for a currently usable password; choose Disabled and submit this action to invalidate its password, once you have confirmed it is you. This does not provision another login method or remove MFA.

items.label: Enable password-based authentication
items.description: Shown for a currently unusable password; once you have confirmed it is you, validates and saves the replacement.

items.label: Breadcrumbs
items.description: Return to the target user, Users list, module or administration home without changing the password.

sections.title: Recorded effect
paragraphs: A successful change, enable or disable operation records an attributed account.password_changed audit event and Django administration log entry without secret values. If changing your own password, Django updates this session’s authentication hash to preserve it. Only the password is saved: laboratory roles, capabilities, the client link and Active do not change, and a deactivation or other account change saved by someone else while this form was open is kept. No user invitation or password notification email is sent by this maintenance form. A save refused because the confirmation was missing or not accepted records nothing.
